question: Which biological learning mechanisms have inspired artificial neural-network algorithms, what engineering benefits might they offer, and where do their scalability claims remain weak?

key_findings.claim: The review organizes brain learning as interactions among local synaptic plasticity and broader modulatory, metaplastic, structural, and cellular processes rather than as one canonical update rule.
key_findings.evidence: It surveys short- and long-term plasticity, neuromodulation, metaplasticity, adult neurogenesis, and glial regulation, emphasizing that biological adaptation emerges across multiple spatial and temporal scales.

anchors.section: Processes that support learning in the brain

key_findings.claim: Local credit-assignment methods remove particular biological implausibilities of backpropagation but retain important accuracy, timing, or supervision constraints.
key_findings.evidence: Feedback alignment replaces transported symmetric weights but underperforms on harder datasets; e-prop maintains forward eligibility traces but still needs real-time learning signals and cannot naturally incorporate delayed errors beyond neuronal timescales.

key_findings.claim: Meta-optimized plasticity is presented as a compromise: a global outer optimizer discovers a local online update rule, but transfer outside the meta-training distribution is unresolved.
key_findings.evidence: The review connects differentiable Hebbian plasticity, evolved learning rules, self-referential updates, and recurrent shared meta-learners; it explicitly notes that larger unconstrained rule spaces make generalization more difficult.

key_findings.claim: The proposed application case is strongest for energy-constrained online adaptation, yet the review supplies no unified quantitative comparison proving brain-inspired rules outperform conventional training.
key_findings.evidence: Neuromorphic hardware, adaptive robotics, and continual learning are surveyed as promising uses; the conclusion argues for more biologically authentic learning, but evidence is assembled from heterogeneous studies rather than a controlled meta-analysis.

method.core_idea: Synthesize biological mechanisms, ANN learning rules, and application areas into a cross-disciplinary taxonomy of brain-inspired learning.
method.mechanism: Narratively connect neuroscience accounts of plasticity to spiking networks, Hebbian/STDP rules, feedback alignment, eligibility propagation, evolutionary search, differentiable plasticity, self-referential meta-learning, neuromorphic chips, robotics, and continual learning.
assumptions: Biological plausibility can yield engineering benefits beyond explanatory neuroscience.
Local plasticity and neuromodulation are transferable abstractions across biological and artificial substrates.
Results from heterogeneous tasks and hardware platforms can support broad qualitative conclusions.
Online adaptation and energy efficiency are central limitations of conventional ANNs.

techniques.role: Relates synaptic, modulatory, structural, and population-level learning mechanisms.
Covers feedback alignment and eligibility traces that reduce global weight transport.
Uses outer-loop gradient or evolutionary optimization to discover online local rules.
Maps learning mechanisms to neuromorphic hardware, robotics, and lifelong learning.

evaluations.setting: Narrative review of approximately 150 cited works
evaluations.metric: Coverage of biological mechanisms, algorithms, and applications
evaluations.result: Provides a broad conceptual map from synapses to hardware and robotics
evaluations.baseline: Single-mechanism reviews of SNNs, continual learning, or neuromorphic systems

evaluations.setting: Scalability evidence summarized for feedback alignment variants
evaluations.result: FA works on small vision tasks but often trails backpropagation on ImageNet; sign-symmetry variants are reported as more competitive
Shared recurrent rules can generalize in selected studies, while broad unconstrained search remains difficult

limitations: This is a narrative rather than systematic review: no search protocol, inclusion criteria, quality grading, or effect-size synthesis is reported.
Biological plausibility, hardware efficiency, continual retention, and task accuracy are distinct objectives that are sometimes discussed together.
Many cited benefits come from small or specialized demonstrations rather than matched modern-scale baselines.
Mechanistic neuroscience remains uncertain, so biological fidelity is itself difficult to validate.
Several conclusions are forward-looking advocacy rather than empirically adjudicated comparisons.
failure_modes: A locally available rule can be biologically plausible yet poorly aligned with the task gradient.
Outer-loop meta-learning hides substantial global computation behind an online-local inner rule.
Neuromorphic energy gains can disappear after including encoding, memory, and training overhead.
Rules optimized on a narrow task family can fail catastrophically under new temporal statistics.
Adding biological detail may increase complexity without improving either neuroscience fidelity or engineering performance.
reusable_insights: Evaluate brain-inspired methods on separate axes: locality, temporal credit, energy, accuracy, continual retention, and transfer.
Account for the outer-loop cost when calling a learned plasticity rule local or efficient.
Use large, architecture-matched benchmarks before interpreting small-task plausibility as scalability.
open_questions: Which local rules retain accuracy and transfer at transformer or large-scale vision scale?
How should biological fidelity be operationalized independently of engineering utility?
Can neuromorphic online learning beat conventional accelerators on end-to-end energy and latency?

competitive_landscape.title: Assessing the Scalability of Biologically-Motivated Deep Learning Algorithms and Architectures
competitive_landscape.difference: Bartunov et al. rigorously test target propagation and feedback alignment through ImageNet and find large gaps; the reviewed paper covers a wider mechanism space but does not reproduce that controlled evaluation.

competitive_landscape.title: Differentiable plasticity: training plastic neural networks with backpropagation
competitive_landscape.difference: Miconi et al. experimentally optimize Hebbian plastic connections for memory and RL; the review places this hybrid global-local method among many brain-inspired routes and highlights generalization as an open issue.

competitive_landscape.title: A solution to the learning dilemma for recurrent networks of spiking neurons
competitive_landscape.difference: Bellec et al. derive and test e-prop for recurrent SNNs; the review summarizes its forward eligibility traces while noting dependence on contemporaneous learning signals.

competitive_landscape.title: Continual Lifelong Learning with Neural Networks: A Review
competitive_landscape.difference: Parisi et al. systematically focus on continual-learning mechanisms and catastrophic forgetting; the reviewed paper spans a broader neuroscience-to-hardware landscape with less depth on any one benchmark taxonomy.

novelty_assessment: Its contribution is breadth and an accessible crosswalk, not a new learning algorithm or decisive systematic evidence. The most research-useful conclusion is that local, meta-optimized, and neuromorphic approaches require multidimensional evaluation; the advocacy for biological authenticity should remain separate from claims of scale or superiority.
reviewer_notes: Read the complete review, with particular attention to local credit assignment, meta-optimized plasticity, applications, and conclusion. Direct primary arXiv records for the main scalability, plasticity, e-prop, and continual-learning comparisons were checked on 2026-08-23.
